clue.text: Songwriter who was dubious poet

parts.note: Bob Dylan is the famous American songwriter
Doubting Thomas was the apostle who doubted the resurrection

explanation.surface: A songwriter is described as a questionable poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sneer at Bob Dylan's verse; in fact the clue joins Dylan to doubting Thomas to name the Welsh poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Dylan Thomas was a celebrated Welsh writer of verse, author of Under Milk Wood.

clue.text: The exact item

parts.note: exact means definite, precise
an item is an article, a single thing

explanation.surface: A phrase for the precise object in question.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue looks like a definition of something precise, but 'The' is the definition: grammarians call it this.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the word 'the' is classed as this, as opposed to 'a' or 'an'.

clue.text: Frenchman about to find riches

parts.note: Luc is a common French man's name
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is about to strike it rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money or wealth, usually with a sense of greed, as in filthy lucre.

clue.text: Iron and tungsten are recycled near Chinese city

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and remade, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: W is the chemical symbol for tungsten

explanation.surface: Scrap metals are being recycled close to a city in China.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Chinese city' as one phrase, but 'Chinese' gives CH and 'city' alone is the definition; 'are recycled' rearranges IRON and W.
explanation.definitionFit: Norwich is a cathedral city in Norfolk, in the east of England.

clue.text: Hollywood's top director exhibiting arrogance

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, here of Hollywood

parts.note: an auteur is a film director with a strong personal style

explanation.surface: A leading Hollywood director shows arrogance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top director' looks like one phrase, but 'top' takes the first letter of Hollywood.
explanation.definitionFit: Hauteur is haughtiness, a proud and superior manner.

clue.text: Part of Ireland consuming a quarter of Edam's cheese

indicators.note: consuming means eating, so one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: Munster is one of the four provinces of Ireland

indicators.note: Edam has four letters, so a quarter of it is its first letter

explanation.surface: An Irish province eats some Dutch cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edam's cheese' looks like one phrase, but Edam only supplies E and 'cheese' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Muenster is a mild, soft cheese, originally from Alsace, also spelt Munster.

clue.text: He may improve expression if he practises the piano, perhaps

definitions.text: He may improve expression if he practises the piano, perhaps

parts.words: He may improve expression if he practises the piano, perhaps
parts.note: the surface suggests a pianist polishing musical expression, but the expression meant is spoken, improved by a clinical professional

explanation.surface: A musician hopes piano practice will make their playing more expressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expression' and 'piano' point to music; the clue really describes a professional who treats problems with speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: This professional helps people improve how they speak and express themselves.

clue.text: Son frequently showing temper

parts.note: frequently means often

explanation.surface: A boy keeps losing his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temper' reads as an angry mood, but here it is the verb meaning to moderate.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to moderate or tone it down, a synonym of making it less harsh.

clue.text: Behind top part of a horse's anatomy

parts.note: A is top grade, first-class, as in A1
the stern is the hindquarters or rear of an animal

explanation.surface: A rear end described as the upper part of a horse's body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a noun for a backside, which fits the horse, but it is the adverb meaning at the back, as on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern means at or towards the back, especially of a ship.

clue.text: Functionary put in charge in advance

indicators.note: put here means placed, with the second 'in' saying where: inside another piece

parts.note: an advance is an offer, as in making advances

explanation.surface: An official is appointed to run things ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in charge' reads as appointing someone, but 'in charge' is the abbreviation and 'put ... in' is the container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer is an official holding a post, a functionary in an organisation.

clue.text: Reduce consumption to no avail

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase, matching the adjective used predicatively, as in 'it was useless'

parts.note: consumption means use
to reduce is to make less

explanation.surface: Cutting back on consumption achieved nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduce consumption' sounds like advice to cut back; the pieces join in the opposite order to the clue's words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done to no avail has no effect, so it is futile and pointless.

clue.text: Orange, brown and green iodine compound

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: a compound mixes ingredients together, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A list of colours and a chemical compound of iodine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' plays on chemistry with iodine but signals an anagram of GREEN and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small citrus fruit, a kind of orange.

clue.text: Safe contains cents in South American currency

indicators.note: contains means one piece holds another

parts.note: safe means sure, certain

explanation.surface: A strongbox is holding small coins in a Latin American money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe' looks like a strongbox, but it is the adjective meaning sure.
explanation.definitionFit: The sucre was the currency of Ecuador until it adopted the US dollar in 2000.

clue.text: A, B, C, D, F or G?

definitions.text: A, B, C, D, F or G?

parts.words: A, B, C, D, F or G?
parts.note: these are musical pitches, each named by a letter; the one letter missing from the list is E

explanation.surface: A question listing letters, as if a multiple-choice answer.
explanation.walkthrough: Each listed letter names a musical pitch, and the list omits E: read the answer as NOT E.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of these letters names a musical pitch, a single sound in the scale.

clue.text: Working hostler can still be found here

definitions.text: Working hostler can still be found here

indicators.note: working means in action, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A city where horse grooms are still employed.
explanation.walkthrough: A hostler is a groom at an inn; Charleston, South Carolina, still runs horse-drawn carriage tours, so the whole clue also defines the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Charleston in South Carolina is known for its horse-drawn carriages, so stable workers still ply their trade there.

clue.text: Taste our fresh fish!

indicators.note: fresh means new, so these letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A fishmonger invites customers to sample the catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' looks like it describes the fish, but it rearranges TASTE OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea trout is a migratory form of brown trout, a game fish.

clue.text: New, rash and mostly wayward English bowler

indicators.note: wayward means erratic, so these letters are rearranged
mostly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A reckless, unpredictable English bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts AND to AN; 'wayward' rearranges NEW, RASH and AN. Shane Warne was in fact Australian, so 'English' only supplies E.
explanation.definitionFit: Shane Warne was a great Australian leg-spin bowler in cricket.

clue.text: American grave contains sixth of victims in TT

indicators.note: in means placed within another piece

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so sober

explanation.surface: A grave holds one of the victims of the TT motorcycle races.
explanation.walkthrough: TT suggests the Isle of Man motorbike races, but here it means teetotal. 'American' signals the US spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Somber is the American spelling of sombre, meaning grave or gloomy.

clue.text: Lithium turned up in food causing illness

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read upwards, so the letters are reversed in place

parts.note: aliment means food or nourishment
Li is the chemical symbol for lithium

explanation.surface: Lithium found in food made someone ill.
explanation.walkthrough: The food is ALIMENT; 'turned up' reverses its LI to IL.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is a minor illness or disorder.

clue.text: Airing disarray about European country

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around another
disarray means disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Airing grievances about a European country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disarray' rearranges AIRING to NIGRIA, and 'about' puts it around E.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria is a large country in West Africa.

clue.text: Coat and belt

definitions.meaning: to move fast or to strike hard

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like clothing; only the first is meant that way.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelt is an animal's skin, and to pelt is to hurtle or to beat, as belt does.

clue.text: No to this clue!

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number, so this asks for the number of this very clue

explanation.surface: An exclamation rejecting the clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' looks like a refusal, but it is No., number: the answer is the clue's own number.
explanation.definitionFit: The number printed beside this clue in the grid is this figure.

clue.text: It's sung a second before New Year in Vietnam

indicators.note: before places one piece in front of the other

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
Tet is the Vietnamese New Year festival

explanation.surface: Something is sung just before the Vietnamese New Year.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short choral composition, often sacred, for unaccompanied voices.

clue.text: Stage after which I propose to make laws

parts.note: a stage of a journey is a leg
to slate someone is to propose them as a candidate, especially in American usage

explanation.surface: Someone sets out the stage after which they will propose new laws.
explanation.walkthrough: SLATE in the sense of propose or nominate is mainly American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make or enact laws.

clue.text: Me, say

definitions.meaning: ME is the postal abbreviation for Maine
to say is to declare or put into words

explanation.walkthrough: 'Me' looks like the pronoun, but it is the abbreviation for Maine.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is an American state, and to state something is to say it.

clue.text: Ring for nurse before the end

indicators.note: before places one piece in front of the other

parts.note: EN is the abbreviation for enrolled nurse
the close is the end, as in the close of day

explanation.surface: Calling a nurse before the end of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like telephoning, but it is the verb meaning to encircle.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring something is to surround it, to encircle or fence it in.

clue.text: He's down-to-earth about the rich and famous

parts.note: re means about, concerning
the A-list is the set of top celebrities

explanation.surface: A grounded person is talking about celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist is a practical person who sees things as they are, a down-to-earth sort.

clue.text: He sells property and car to a nice chap

parts.note: an estate is a British name for a station wagon car
a gent is a gentleman, a nice chap

explanation.surface: A property dealer hands his car over to a pleasant fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British term for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate agent is the British name for a realtor who sells houses.
